xmldoc.short_description: Open tar archive returned by nelson.io.tar.open.

description.p: nelson.io.TarArchive keeps a tar archive open between calls.
Read-only properties: Source (file name or URL, empty for an in-memory archive), Mode ("r" or "w"), Compression ("none", "gzip", "zstd", "xz", "bzip2", "lz4" or "lzma"), Level and IsOpen.
Methods: entries, read, readtext, write, add, fopen, extract, tobytes and close, with the same arguments as the nelson.io.tar functions without the first one.

t.extract(outputfolder, Name, Value) accepts the options MaxExtractedSize (largest total number of bytes written) and MaxCompressionRatio (largest ratio between the total size of the files and the size of the archive file), both Inf by default, like untar. These limits and the free disk space of the destination are checked before anything is written.

The 'Compression' and 'Level' options of nelson.io.tar.open choose how a writer compresses. Levels are 0 to 9 for gzip, xz and lzma, 1 to 9 for bzip2 and lz4, 1 to 22 for zstd, and -1 for the default of the method. zstd and xz compress on several threads (see maxNumCompThreads).

extract restores dates and keeps execute permissions (umask applied), except on Windows. On Linux and macOS, a symbolic link is restored only when its target stays inside the destination folder; other links, hard links, and all links on Windows are skipped. '..' names and writing through symbolic links are refused.
entries returns a table with Name, Size, Modified (a datetime), Mode (unix permission bits as a double), IsFolder and IsLink.
Displaying the object shows these properties. Deleting the object closes the archive; when an entry is still written through a file identifier, the archive is closed when that identifier is closed.
